pairs.reason: Both keep up military pressure and do not pull back early; they differ on agreements, which one refuses for now and the other makes the goal of the pressure.
Both keep force available against attack, but one keeps attacking until the threats are gone and the other stops attacking now even with threats remaining.
One keeps attacking and stays in Lebanon with no deals because only force brings security; the other ends all operations, withdraws now and relies on diplomacy alone.
Both aim at agreed arrangements and keep force in some role, but one keeps attacking until a deal with guarantees is in place and the other stops attacking first.
Both seek regional peace agreements, but one uses continued military pressure and pulls back only after a deal while the other ends operations and withdraws now, using diplomacy alone.
Both stop attacking now and put ending the fighting first; they differ on keeping force to respond to attacks versus withdrawing from Lebanon and relying on diplomacy alone.
